name: nikto
plain: `nikto` asks a web server thousands of questions: does /admin exist, is this old version of Apache vulnerable, is a dangerous file left behind, are risky HTTP methods allowed? It prints every finding it can match against its database.
It is noisy: every probe shows in the server's logs, and many findings are informational. Use it as a quick first sweep on a lab web server, then investigate the interesting lines by hand.
when: Get a quick list of known issues on a lab web server.
Find forgotten files and directories, default pages and risky methods.
Check server headers and outdated software.
Save a report for your notes.

examples.title: Scan a host
examples.explain: -h is the target. Output lines start with + and describe each finding, often with an OSVDB or CVE reference.

examples.title: A different port
examples.explain: -p sets the port (or a list such as 80,8080).

examples.title: Save a report
examples.explain: -o is the file; -Format can be csv, htm, json, txt, xml.

examples.title: Choose test types
examples.explain: Tuning picks categories: 1 interesting files, 2 misconfigurations, 3 information disclosure, 4 injection (XSS), 9 SQL injection, x reverse the selection.

examples.title: Behind a login
examples.explain: Sends HTTP basic authentication with each request.

examples.title: Quieter and slower
examples.explain: Waits between requests and sets the user agent. It does not make the scan invisible.

examples.title: Through a proxy
examples.explain: Sends traffic through Burp so you can see every request.

options.plain: Target host, IP, URL or a file of hosts.
Prepend a base path to every request.
Test categories to run or skip.
Guess file and directory names with extra rules.
Use IDS-evasion tricks for the request.
Report format: csv, htm, json, msf+, nbe, txt, xml.
Control what is printed (1 redirects, 2 cookies, 3 OK, 4 URLs, E errors, V verbose).
Do not look up host names.
Check the databases for syntax errors.

mistakes: Treating every + line as a vulnerability: many are informational.
Running it on a site you do not have permission to scan: it is loud and easily detected.
Forgetting -ssl and getting no results from an HTTPS port.
Scanning only the default port and missing the app on 8080.
try: Scan your own lab web server and sort the findings into 'real' and 'noise'.
Send nikto through Burp and watch the requests it makes.
see_also: gobuster(1), ffuf(1), wfuzz(1), dirb(1), curl(1), nmap(1) (http-* scripts), burpsuite.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
